clusters.name: Domain Data Access Abstraction Patterns
clusters.description: Architectural decisions on how the platform encapsulates reads/writes for core domain entities using abstraction layers like repositories.

relations.rationale: User-interaction flows (e.g., order history, subscriptions) typically rely on consistent domain data access abstractions.

values.label: Repository pattern for key domain entities
values.description: Use repositories to centralize querying/operations for entities such as user profiles, meal orders, and meals.

values.label: Repository pattern for orders, promotions, subscriptions
values.description: Apply repositories to transactional and offer-related data to decouple data-access logic from business logic.

clusters.name: User Interface Flow Architecture for Features
clusters.description: Decisions about structuring user interaction flows (UI vs controllers/services) for feature modules like browsing, history, and subscriptions.

values.label: Adopt MVC for browsing/history/subscription flows
values.description: Use MVC architecture to manage separation of concerns for UI and interaction flows across those features.

clusters.name: Search and Filtering Rule Modeling
clusters.description: How meal discovery/query constraints are represented—i.e., rule composition for availability and dietary criteria.

values.label: Specification objects for filtering criteria
values.description: Model search filtering via specification objects that compose availability and dietary constraints.

clusters.name: Third-Party Map Provider Integration Strategy
clusters.description: How external map/location services are integrated: providing consistent interfaces, isolating provider APIs, and supporting swaps.

relations.rationale: Interfaces/facades enable runtime strategy swapping of map/search components without exposing provider details.

values.label: Adapter pattern for multi-map provider integration
values.description: Integrate multiple map providers behind common contracts using adapters.

values.label: Facade layer for external map abstraction
values.description: Use a facade to isolate and standardize interactions with external map providers for discovery workflows.

clusters.name: Pluggable Component Selection via Runtime Strategies
clusters.description: How the system selects implementations at runtime (e.g., map provider or search algorithm), emphasizing configurability/extensibility.

relations.rationale: Runtime swapping typically requires a stable abstraction layer (adapter/facade) to interchange implementations safely.

values.label: Strategy pattern for runtime map/search swapping
values.description: Use Strategy to dynamically swap map providers or search algorithms at runtime.

clusters.name: Registration Workflow State and Validation Design
clusters.description: How user sign-up is implemented as a multi-step process, including validation gates and explicit confirmation.

values.label: Multi-step registration with validation and confirmation
values.description: Implement registration as multiple steps with form validation at steps and a final confirmation step.

saturation_history.rationale:
All provided open codes are already covered by existing taxonomy dimensions:
- Registration flow, validation, and confirmation are fully captured by dimension 6 ("Multi-step registration with validation and confirmation").
- Repository pattern for domain data operations, including users/meal orders/meals and also orders/promotions/subscriptions, is covered by dimension 1 (with values 1.1 and 1.2).
- Adopting MVC for browsing/history/subscription interaction flows is covered by dimension 2 (value 2.1).
- Meal search filtering via specification objects for availability + dietary criteria is covered by dimension 3 (value 3.1).
- Adapter pattern and facade layer for external map provider abstraction, plus Strategy pattern for runtime map/search swapping, are covered by dimensions 4 and 5 (values 4.1, 4.2, and 5.1).
Since every relevant open code maps cleanly to an existing dimension/value without introducing a new architectural axis, the taxonomy is saturated for this minibatch.

All open codes in the minibatch are already covered by existing taxonomy dimensions: (1) “Encrypted credential storage for user passwords” and (2) “Strict access controls on credential storage” are subsumed by Dimension 7 (Credential Storage and Access Control), whose value 7.1 explicitly covers encrypted storage plus strict access controls. (3) “Observer pattern for propagating subscription/promotion plan changes to UI” is directly covered by Dimension 9 (Client-Side Plan Change Propagation Mechanisms), value 9.1. (4) “Adopt standard credential-based authentication” is covered by Dimension 8 (Credential-Based Authentication Mechanism), value 8.1. (5) “Adopted MVC for core user-interaction flows” is covered by Dimension 2 (User Interface Flow Architecture for Features), value 2.1. Since every minibatch code maps cleanly to an existing dimension axis, the taxonomy is saturated for this minibatch.
